problem: Prior robot-navigation surveys cover classical, hand-crafted methods, and there was no comprehensive overview of deep-learning methods for embodied visual navigation across simulators, tasks, metrics, cross-modal instruction following and sim-to-real transfer.
motivation: Embodied navigation needs perception, mapping, exploration, memory, language grounding and adaptation, and the literature is scattered across many tasks and simulators. A unified taxonomy helps newcomers and shows where the field falls short of human-level, real-world navigation.
key_idea: Organize deep-learning embodied navigation into a taxonomy of environments, benchmarks and metrics, methods in simulation (target-driven and cross-modal), and real-world / sim-to-real methods, then draw out open challenges.
insight: The survey argues that auxiliary self-supervised tasks, map or topological memory, and pretrained transformers (PREVALENT, VLN-BERT) drive the largest gains. Its R2R table shows a gap to humans (63 SR / 57 SPL vs 86 / 76) that persists even for the best model. Sim-to-real is hindered by differences in observation, action space and dynamics. This is a literature review with no ablations of its own.
method: Environments: compares datasets (SUNCG, Matterport3D, Gibson, Replica) and simulators (MINOS, AI2-THOR, Habitat, iGibson) by resolution, FPS, physics, interactivity and multi-agent support.

Benchmarks and metrics: categorizes tasks as target-driven (PointGoal, ObjectGoal, RoomGoal, MultiON), cross-modal (VLN, NDH, EQA, REVERIE, audio-visual) or interactive (IQA, HANNA); compares metrics (SR, SPL, SED, CLS, nDTW) on path similarity, penalties, optimum and complexity.
Target-driven methods: reviews model-free (A3C, IL+RL), self-supervised auxiliary-task and planning-based (neural SLAM, ANS, topological SLAM, SemExp) approaches.
Cross-modal methods: reviews seq2seq/speaker-follower/RL, pretraining (PREVALENT, VLN-BERT, recurrent VLN-BERT), EQA/QA and dialogue-based navigation.
Real world and sim-to-real: reviews indoor, outdoor and long-range robots, analyzes the domain gap (observation, action, dynamics) and covers transfer methods.
Future directions: richer environments, better-defined tasks and metrics, stronger performance, language perception, and robust real-world deployment.

setting.simulator: n/a (survey covers Habitat, Matterport3D, AI2-THOR, iGibson etc.)

numbers_note: Survey with no own method. It reproduces a table of other methods' R2R results (baselines) and Habitat challenge bar charts, which are excluded.
results: The survey reports that the best R2R model (recurrent VLN-BERT) reaches 63 SR and 57 SPL on test unseen, versus human 86 SR and 76 SPL. It also cites Habitat PointGoal at 64.5 SR / 37.7 SPL and ObjectGoal at 21.08 SR / 8.38 SPL, all still far from human level.
limitations: Coverage stops at 2021 and covers no LLM or foundation-model navigation.
Descriptive rather than quantitative; there is no unified benchmark comparison, and results appear only for R2R and in figures.
Some descriptions and citations are imprecise, and the real-world sections are relatively thin.
compares_to: Prior robot navigation surveys (DeSouza & Kak, Kruse et al.)
